newsitem.title: UK: HeavyLift flights beating Spanish truckers' strike.
newsitem.headline: HeavyLift flights beating Spanish truckers' strike.

text.p: HeavyLift Cargo Airlines has so far carried around 1,000 tonnes of cargo on a dozen flights to help motor manufacturers and importers of perishable goods beat the effects of the Spanish truckers' strike, HeavyLift spokesman Vince Seeger told Reuters.
The flights using both Antonov-124 and Ilyushin-76 freighters had moved a wide range of automotive parts including engines, gear boxes, steering wheels and windscreen sets.
"Bookings are still coming in today," Seeger added.
Outward bound flights from Spain have been almost evenly split between Britain and Germany, he said but declined to identify the manufacturers involved.
A further 200 tonnes of automotive parts have been flown into Spain, he said.
"There have also been a few flights within Spain itself, with helicopters used for moving freight," he said.
Flights from Barcelona and Lisbon have also been used the Ilyushin's to move fish exports to France, Seeger added.
Heavylift is based at Stansted in the UK and specialises in heavy and outsize shipments. It is part of the Traflagar House group, itself controlled by Kvaerner A/S.
